title: The Board's votes on labor agreements
question: How many ordinances adopting labor agreements (Memoranda of Understanding) are on file, how many carry a roll call on disk, and did any draw a no vote?
finding: 218 ordinances adopting or implementing a labor agreement are in the Board's legislation records; 1 has a roll call on disk, and it drew a no: file 220594 (San Francisco Police Officers Association), finally passed 9-1, no from Dean Preston. Timing (a question only): Carpenters gave $291,000 a year in agreement years and the year before, against $63,046 in other years.
how: Legislation records whose type is Ordinance and whose title adopts or implements a Memorandum of Understanding; the party is read from the title. Roll calls and members' votes are this site's Board-vote tables, which cover contracts, grants, leases, appropriations and lobbied measures, not every ordinance. The timing line sets a family's yearly giving (the “unions” results) in the years an agreement passed, and the year before, against its other years since 2015.
limits: Missing roll calls are a gap in what was downloaded, not secret votes; nearly all ordinances pass unanimously. Agreements are negotiated by the Department of Human Resources and some are arbitration awards the Board must implement. Election years drive giving; a match of years is not evidence of an exchange.
